name: What is the best way to evaluate a multifamily development site before buying it?

mainEntity.name: What due diligence should a buyer do before purchasing Los Angeles apartment land?
mainEntity.text: What due diligence should a buyer do before purchasing Los Angeles apartment land?

acceptedAnswer.text: A strong pre-purchase review is the difference between a viable project and an expensive mistake. Buyers should evaluate zoning, allowable density, setbacks, height, parking, access, utility capacity, geotechnical conditions, title restrictions, easements, and likely permit hurdles. The development team should also test whether the project works financially at conservative rent and cost assumptions, not just optimistic ones. In Los Angeles-area markets, even a small issue such as an easement, slope, or utility conflict can reshape the entire project. A feasibility study should include conceptual site plans, a rough budget, and a schedule estimate before closing. If the site only works with ideal market conditions, it may not be a good acquisition. The best buyers treat due diligence as a way to eliminate uncertainty before they commit to a land basis that cannot be recovered.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best site review checks zoning, parking, access, setbacks, utility capacity, soil conditions, title issues, neighbor impacts, and financial feasibility. A site can look ideal on a map but fail once design and cost are tested. Early due diligence should confirm that the parcel can support the desired unit count and construction type.
